title: CGELBank treebank, JSON-LD serialization
description: A corpus of CGEL constituency trees. Mirrors the PENMAN-style .cgel format read by cgel.py: each level of indentation in the .cgel source becomes one level of nesting under `children`. Generated and validated by cgel2jsonld.py.

@context.description: JSON-LD context. Emitted inline so documents are self-contained; may also be an IRI.

tree.description: One sentence: its `# key = value` header lines plus the tree itself.

source.description: Path of the .cgel file this tree was read from.

text.description: Convenience copy of the `text` header: the sentence with original punctuation.

sent.description: Convenience copy of the `sent` header: whitespace-tokenized terminals.

metadata.description: Every `# key = value` header line, in source order. Authoritative: the convenience properties above are derived from these, and round-tripping back to .cgel uses only this list.

node.description: A constituent. Nonterminals carry `children`; terminals carry `text`; gaps carry neither.

function.$comment: Closed inventory: every function occurring in datasets/**/*.cgel as of CGELBank 1.0, plus Mod_ext, which cgel.py recognizes (Node.isMod) but the corpus does not yet use. A `+` joins fused functions; `-` joins a function to a nucleus role. Extend this list when the annotation manual adds a function.
function.description: Grammatical function relating this node to its parent, i.e. the `:Deprel` in the .cgel source. Absent on the root, and only on the root.

category.$comment: Closed inventory: every category occurring in datasets/**/*.cgel as of CGELBank 1.0. A `+` marks a fused category (NP+PP is a fused relative etc.); `_` marks a subtype (V_aux, N_pro, Clause_rel, PP_strand). Extend this list when the annotation manual adds a category.
category.description: Syntactic category, i.e. the constituent label, or the literal "GAP" for a gap node.

index.description: Coindexation variable. On a non-GAP node it marks an antecedent; on a GAP node it names the antecedent being pointed at.

antecedent.description: Resolved link from a gap to its antecedent node. Derived from `index`; omitted if the antecedent cannot be resolved within the tree.

text.description: Surface form of a terminal (`:t`). Its presence is what makes a node lexical.

position.description: 1-based index of this terminal among the tree's terminals, in surface order. Derived, not present in the .cgel source.

lemma.description: Explicit lemma (`:l`), present only where it differs from the surface form. Consumers wanting a lemma for every terminal should fall back to `correct`, then `text`.

correct.description: Normalization of a misspelled or erroneous token (`:correct`). The empty string marks a spurious token to be deleted, and is meaningfully different from this property being absent.

prePunct.description: Punctuation (`:p`) attached before this terminal, in order.

postPunct.description: Punctuation (`:p`) attached after this terminal, in order.

subtokens.description: Decomposition of a complex lexeme into subtokens (`:subt`) and subpunctuation (`:subp`), in order.

children.description: Child constituents in surface order. One level of indentation in the .cgel source. Absent or empty on terminals and gaps.

allOf.$comment: A gap is a leaf: it has no surface form and no children.
Only a lexical node can carry a surface position, punctuation or subtokens.
A node cannot be both lexical and branching.

kind.description: `subt` for a subtoken, `subp` for internal punctuation.
